attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's P0 against INV-R7.3, adopted whole. T?(∅) = ∅ and T?(S) = ⊤ for S ≠ ∅ — the least informative conservative transfer, rather than identity. Applies in four places, all executed: an edge with no transfer, an edge whose transfer is declared but not discharged, an input set matched by no rule on a non-additive edge, and a kind with no singleton rule on an edge that IS declared additive. scripts/emb-impact-closure.mjs §3 seeds SINGLETONS, which is precisely what R7.3 never did: {correctness}, {authority} and {confidentiality} each go to ⊤ and ∅ stays ∅. §5 carries the meta-check GPT-5.6 asked for — a control set with no non-⊤ seed is refused, because R7.3's suite could only test at the top, where identity and ⊤ agree. §5 also runs the end-to-end consequence: a {correctness} seed now reaches A-REPORT in AUTHORITY, which under R7.3 it did not. CORRECTED AT R7.5. This claim names FOUR situations that produce ⊤ and R7.4 could exhibit THREE: the fourth, `a kind with no singleton rule on an edge that IS declared additive`, had no witness because the fixture contained no declared-additive edge anywhere — it was a sentence with no code path under it, and the mutant that makes that branch return ∅ instead of ⊤ (M10, the UNSOUND direction) survived the R7.4 suite. E9 is the first additive edge in the fixture. §1 now refuses any applies_to entry without an edge that exhibits it, which replaces R7.4’s /T\?\(S\)\s*=\s*⊤/.test(IA.unknown_transfer.rule) — A REGEX OVER A REGISTRY STRING, in the round whose finding was that the registry sentence and the executable disagreed.

attrs.review_focus: Safety here is bought by giving up all precision, and that is the honest trade rather than a temporary one: precision returns only when a narrowing is DISCHARGED, and nothing in this artifact has ever discharged one. A reader who sees ⊤ everywhere is seeing the correct answer.
